render_brief.form: Plain, slightly flared hollow tumbler, smoothly rounded lip, thick closed transparent base. No stem, handle, cuts, flutes, modern logo, printed graduations or invented brand.
render_brief.reconstruction: Precise profile, wall thickness, 1.4 cm inner floor height, fill level and numeric colour values are reconstructions. Nominal gill size is period terminology, not a claim of a calibrated modern measure.
render_brief.colour: Colourless transparent glass, warm full-colour amber liquid at roughly one-third of the inner height. Amber is an interpretation supported by the existing period whiskey-colouring research; no colourimetry claim.
render_brief.presentation: Enlarged 4.5x as a readable currency game piece, resting on an existing sourced whiskey barrel at the supply line. Enlargement is game convention, not historical scale. No character drinks or holds it.
render_brief.native_guard: Any source or recipient with a public Native visual uses the existing plain-crate supply scene and neutral caption instead. Never read hidden identity.

history_lines: McKee's 1868 list sold small plain bar tumblers.
An 1884 bar manual used a small glass for whiskey.
This plain profile and amber fill are reconstructed.
